answer: Admission proof-of-work at the karst gateway: each identity must submit a puzzle costing ~480 CPU-hours. The inlet throttles submissions to one per wallet per epoch, so a farm of 1000 sybils burns ~480,000 CPU-hours (~$9,600 at cloud spot rates) before earning one vote. The canyon between honest single-node cost and farm cost widens linearly — no economy of scale exists since puzzles are independently seeded. Attackers face rising marginal cost with zero marginal reward, so flooding stays unprofitable. This works because the proof is unforgeable, non-parallelizable per identity, and priced.
